title: KPMG: enterprise agent governance and lifecycle management
source_category: Named-customer adoption announcement, not a measured production workflow
availability: Announced adoption; rollout completion not independently verified
overview: KPMG and Microsoft announced Agent 365 adoption to govern agent deployment, management, monitoring and updates across KPMG, alongside Copilot expansion. This case models those stated lifecycle operations, not an invented audit-client transaction.
published_facts: The Microsoft press release explicitly names KPMG's adoption of Agent 365.
The stated use is governance of agent deployment, management, monitoring and updates.
The announcement connects this work with KPMG's Trusted AI framework and Workbench platform.

sources.title: KPMG and Microsoft scale trusted, enterprise AI agents globally through deployment of Agent 365 and Copilot
sources.verification: Primary page fetched and read by the research agent; reported HTTP 200.

a365_relationship: Direct: the announcement explicitly names Microsoft Agent 365. It does not establish that every member firm's rollout is complete.
intent: Bring an enterprise agent into managed deployment, monitor its activity and apply a governed lifecycle update.
actors: Enterprise governance administrators and the managed agent; local model role GovernanceAgent abstracts their workflow.
published_outcome: An announced governed agent operating model; no independently observed completion rate or security effectiveness is claimed here.

actions.description: Prepare an agent for managed enterprise deployment.
Deploy the prepared agent under enterprise management.
Apply a managed lifecycle update to the agent.

local_assumptions: The four named capabilities and their sequential effects are local abstractions, not KPMG API names or a published KPMG execution protocol.
The declared environment grants each modeled lifecycle operation; actual tenant grants and rollout state are unknown.
Independent approval of the exact lifecycle update is an added local runtime test policy, not a stated KPMG approval procedure.
limitations: SkillC cannot establish rollout completion or query KPMG's private registry.
The checker does not validate the meaning or completeness of KPMG governance controls.
Actual Entra permissions, authenticated approvers and lifecycle API execution need a trusted host adapter.
